extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for obtaining a filing date and for completion/treatment of U.S. patent applications (nonprovisional, provisional, continuation/divisional, and CPA), including fee, oath/declaration, omitted pages, conversion, and notification rules under 37 CFR 1.53 and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely payment of required fees to avoid abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees required by §§ 1.16(h), (i) and (j) (e.g., excess claims or multiple dependent claim fees), the application size fee required by § 1.16(s), basic filing fee (§ 1.16(d)), and applicable surcharges must be paid or the claims canceled by amendment prior to the expiration of the time period set for reply by the Office in any notice of fee deficiency to avoid abandonment. If applicant does not pay the basic filing fee during the pendency of the application, the Office may dispose of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For provisional applications missing cover sheet or basic filing fee, applicant will be notified and given time to pay basic filing fee, file cover sheet, and pay surcharge required by § 1.16(g) (see 37 CFR 1.53(g)); if no correspondence address provided applicant has two months from the filing date to do so. For applications accorded a filing date under 1.53(b)/(d), fees (basic filing, search, examination) and oath/declaration can be submitted after filing date but missing fees may trigger a surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) depending on filing date and effective dates noted (exceptions for certain filing windows e.g., prior to July 1, 2005). Time periods typically set are 2 months from mailing date of notification and may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Failure to timely pay required fees or surcharges may result in disposal or abandonment; retain handling/refund rules (37 CFR 1.21(n), 1.19(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date requirements for nonprovisional applications (37 CFR 1.53(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.53(b), a filing date is assigned to a nonprovisional application as of the date a specification containing a description and claim and any necessary drawings are filed in the USPTO. Failure to meet any of the requirements in 37 CFR 1.53(b) will result in the application being denied a filing date. The filing date to be accorded such an application is the date on which all of the requirements of 37 CFR 1.53(b) are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing fee, search fee and examination fee for an application filed under 1.53(b) and the oath or declaration can be submitted after the filing date, but no amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure after the filing date. If an application accorded a filing date lacks parts, applicant will be notified and given time to file missing parts (generally 2 months). Applicants should submit copies of notices and include application number on correspondence to aid processing. See related provisions 37 CFR 1.53(e),(f) and MPEP guidance on handling missing parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date requirements for provisional applications (37 CFR 1.53(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application will be given a filing date as of the date the written description and any necessary drawings are filed in the Office pursuant to 37 CFR 1.53(c). Provisional filing date requirements parallel nonprovisional requirements except that no claim is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All provisional applications must be filed with a cover sheet (may be an application data sheet under 37 CFR 1.76 or a cover letter identifying the application as provisional per 1.51(c)(1)). If missing cover sheet or basic filing fee, applicant will be notified and given time (usually 2 months) to file cover sheet, pay basic filing fee and surcharge under 1.16(g) to avoid abandonment. Amendments (other than to comply with regulations) are not permitted after the provisional filing date. The basic filing fee must be paid on filing or within the time under 1.53(g) if any claim for benefit under 35 U.S.C.119(e) based on that provisional application is to be made in a subsequent nonprovisional (see 37 CFR 1.78(a)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion from nonprovisional to provisional (37 CFR 1.53(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under paragraph (b) may be converted to a provisional application and be accorded the original filing date of the application filed under paragraph (b). The request for conversion must be accompanied by the processing fee set forth in § 1.17(q) and be filed prior to the earliest of abandonment, payment of the issue fee, expiration of twelve months after the filing date, or filing a request for a statutory invention registration under § 1.293. Grant of such request does not entitle applicant to a refund of the fees properly paid in the nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converting a nonprovisional to a provisional will not avoid publication unless recognized in sufficient time to remove the nonprovisional from publication; the Office cannot ensure removal if publication process initiated. Conversion disregards priority/benefit claims submitted in the nonprovisional. Applicants filing conversion requests by mail should designate “Mail Stop Conversion.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion from provisional to nonprovisional (37 CFR 1.53(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application may be converted to a nonprovisional application and accorded the original filing date of the provisional. The conversion must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.17(i) and an amendment including at least one claim as prescribed by the second paragraph of 35 U.S.C.112 unless the provisional already contains such a claim. The resulting nonprovisional must include the filing fee, search fee, examination fee, an oath or declaration pursuant to §§ 1.63, 1.162, or 1.175, and the surcharge required by § 1.16(f) if applicable. The request must be filed prior to abandonment of the provisional or expiration of twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion affects patent term: the term of any patent issuing from the application will be measured from at least the filing date of the provisional; applicants should consider claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C.119(e) instead, which is less expensive and results in a longer patent term. No refund of provisional fees; time limits are strict. See MPEP for practical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (continuation/divisional of design applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.53(d) may be used to file either a continuation or a divisional application (but not a continuation-in-part) of a design application. The prior nonprovisional application must be a design application complete as defined by 37 CFR 1.51(b). Any application filed under 1.53(d) must disclose and claim only subject matter disclosed in the prior nonprovisional application and must name as inventors the same or less than all inventors named in the prior application. Under 1.53(d) the filing date assigned is the date on which a request, on a separate paper, for an application under 1.53(d) is filed; the application must be filed before payment of the issue fee on the prior application, abandonment, or termination of proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing fee, search fee and examination fee and the oath/declaration for an application filed under 1.53(b) or 1.53(d) can be submitted after the filing date. No amendment may introduce new matter after the filing date. See MPEP §201.06(d) for CPA limitations and related practice changes (e.g., CPAs limited to design applications effective July 14, 2003).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and cure of incomplete applications (37 CFR 1.53(e) and (f))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.53(e) provides for notifying applicant of any application which is incomplete under 1.53(b) or 1.53(d) and giving the applicant a time period to correct any omission. If the omission is not corrected within the time period given, the application will be returned or otherwise disposed of and a handling fee (37 CFR 1.21(n)) will be retained from any refund of a filing fee. 37 CFR 1.53(f) provides that where a filing date has been assigned, the applicant will be notified (if a correspondence address was provided) and given a period of time to file missing fees, oath/declaration, and to pay any surcharge (37 CFR 1.16(f)) to prevent abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time period usually set is 2 months from mailing date of notification; this period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a). If no correspondence address is included, applicant has 2 months from the filing date to file the missing fees, oath/declaration and pay required surcharge to prevent abandonment. Applicants should submit copies of the notice(s) with replies and include the application number on correspondence to expedite matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration requirements and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration filed in reply to a notice under 37 CFR 1.53(f) must be executed by the inventors and must identify the specification and any amendment filed with the specification which includes subject matter not otherwise included in the specification (including claims) or drawings of the application. No new matter may be included after the filing date of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment is filed with the oath/declaration after the filing date, it may be identified but may not include new matter. If the oath/declaration improperly refers to an amendment filed after the filing date which contains new matter, a supplemental oath/declaration will be required pursuant to 37 CFR 1.67(b) deleting the reference. If an amendment is filed the same day the application is filed, it is part of the original papers and new matter is not considered. Alterations prior to execution of the oath and the filing are considered part of the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of applications filed without all pages of specification — notices and applicant options
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP reviews application papers to determine whether all pages of specification are present. If filed without all pages but containing something that can be construed as a written description, at least one drawing figure if necessary, and (for nonprovisional) at least one claim, OPAP will mail a “Notice of Omitted Items” indicating a filing date was accorded but pages are lacking. If the application contains nothing that can be construed as a written description, OPAP will mail a “Notice of Incomplete Application” indicating lack of the specification required by 35 U.S.C.112 and no filing date is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If mailed a Notice of Omitted Item(s), within 2 months applicant may: (A) file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) with fee and evidence that the pages were received (petition fee refunded if successful); (B) submit omitted pages in a nonprovisional application with an oath/declaration and a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 requesting the later filing date (2-month non-extendable); or (C) accept the application as deposited by not filing a petition (constructive acceptance), in which case amendment to renumber pages and cancel incomplete sentences should be made by preliminary amendment prior to first Office action to avoid delay. If the omitted portion is wholly contained in a prior-filed application and priority is claimed, applicant may submit an amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(a) within 2 months. The 2-month period is not extendable under 37 CFR 1.136. For provisional applications the USPTO will generally not grant petitions under 1.182 to accept omitted pages; applicant should file a new provisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for an application to be entitled to a filing date despite omissions and examiner actions
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is entitled to a filing date if the application contains something that can be construed as a written description, at least one drawing figure if necessary under 35 U.S.C.113 (first sentence), and at least one claim. If a Technology Center discovers an application filed without pages and a Notice of Omitted Items was not mailed by OPAP, the examiner should determine whether the application is entitled to a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If entitled to a filing date, the examiner should notify applicant of the omission in the next Office action and require applicant to: (A) accept the application as filed without all pages; (B) file omitted pages with an oath/declaration and a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 requesting the date of submission as the filing date; or (C) file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) with supporting evidence that the pages were deposited with the original filing. The original application papers that are present in the USPTO on the date of deposit form the original disclosure for filing date purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for review of refusal to accord a filing date (37 CFR 1.53(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.53(e)(2) requires that any request for review of a refusal to accord an application a filing date be made by way of a petition accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §506.02 for procedures. Petition must include appropriate evidence (e.g., date-stamped receipts) to establish entitlement to the requested filing date; petition fee will be refunded if petition is granted. The 2-month periods set in Notices (where applicable) are generally not extendable under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) practice and limitations (37 CFR 1.53(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.53(d) sets forth filing date requirements for a Continued Prosecution Application (CPA). A CPA is a nonprovisional application which must be filed on or after December 1, 1997; only a continuation or divisional (not a continuation-in-part) may be filed as a CPA. Effective July 14, 2003, CPA practice under 37 CFR 1.53(d) does not apply to utility and plant applications; CPAs can only be filed in design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §201.06(d) for further details. The filing date assigned for a 1.53(d) application is the date on which the separate request is filed. Applicants should ensure compliance with disclosure and inventor-naming constraints and with the deadlines (before issue fee payment, abandonment, or termination of proceedings) to preserve entitlement to CPA filing.
